READ-ONLY security-readiness audit of the Nxeon hosting platform at /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15, Prisma, Proxmox provisioning, shared hosting, game servers). Do NOT edit/build/migrate/mutate — investigation only.

A prior pentest this session found + fixed a CRITICAL (DB Studio mysql-CLI RCE → now mysql2 protocol driver as scoped user) and several MEDIUMs (coupon race, hostname-claim TOCTOU, SSRF). Your job: (a) CONFIRM those fixes are actually present in current code (lib/hosting-db.ts uses mysql2 over ssh2 forwardOut as the scoped `_mgr` user, no `mysql` CLI for tenant SQL; HostingHostnameClaim unique table; coupon reserve→confirm→release), and (b) hunt for NEW issues.

Cover: auth/session/RBAC (account takeover, priv-esc, IDOR on every `[id]` route/action — ownership checks), tenant isolation (shared hosting: MySQL grant escaping, chroot/open_basedir, file manager traversal), Stripe/webhook signature + price re-derivation, Proxmox API (no shell injection, no VM IDOR), noVNC token scoping, SSRF in free tools/agency scraper, secrets never leaked to client/logs, upload validation, stored XSS.

Also flag the OPERATIONAL risk: there is reportedly an UNIDENTIFIED "auto-promoter" that ships unreviewed code straight to prod (it put a money bug live this session). Look for any cron/systemd/script/agent in the repo or scripts/ that auto-deploys to prod without review, and report what you find (or that you couldn't find it).

Deliverable: findings ranked CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW with file:line, exploit sketch, and fix. Confirm-or-refute each prior fix explicitly. Honest: if solid, say so.

=== promote-production.sh ===
#!/bin/bash
# Promote the currently deployed staging commit to production.
# Verifies staging is healthy, fast-forwards nothing (prod working tree IS the repo),
# then rebuilds + restarts production services.
set -euo pipefail

STG_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon-staging rev-parse HEAD)
PROD_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon rev-parse HEAD)

echo "==> Staging is at:    $STG_COMMIT"
echo "==> Production is at: $PROD_COMMIT"

if ! systemctl is-active -q nxeon-staging-web; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging web service is not running." >&2
  exit 1
fi
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
if [ "$CODE" != "200" ]; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging returns HTTP $CODE." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ "$STG_COMMIT" != "$PROD_COMMIT" ]; then
  echo "Note: production tree is at a different commit than staging."
  echo "Production deploys directly from /opt/nxeon's working tree (main)."
fi

cd /opt/nxeon
echo "==> Installing dependencies (adds any new deps before build)"
# CRITICAL: without this, a commit that adds a new dependency (e.g. imapflow)
# builds against a stale node_modules and fails — which previously aborted the
# promote AFTER the old build was already gone. Always sync deps first.
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -3
echo "==> Building production"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4
# Guard: never restart into an incomplete/failed build. A valid production build
# always writes .next/BUILD_ID; if it's missing the build failed mid-way and the
# old in-memory process is still serving — abort rather than kill it.
if [ ! -s /opt/nxeon/.next/BUILD_ID ]; then
  echo "BUILD FAILED: .next/BUILD_ID missing — NOT restarting (old process left serving)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. Only .next needs to be writable by
# it (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable, and systemd
# injects .env as root. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon/.env 2>/dev/null || true
echo "==> Restarting production services"
systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-web nxeon-worker
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1/)
echo "==> Production responds: HTTP $CODE"
[ "$CODE" = "200" ] || { echo "PRODUCTION UNHEALTHY — check journalctl -u nxeon-web"; exit 1; }
echo "==> Production promote complete"

=== ci.yml ===
name: CI

# Typecheck + unit tests on every push and every pull request. Nothing here
# touches Proxmox, Stripe, Mailcow, a database or the network beyond the npm
# registry: the whole suite is pure functions (test/*.test.ts).
on:
  push:
    branches: ["**"]
  pull_request:
    branches: ["**"]

# A newer push to the same ref cancels the older run.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  check:
    name: typecheck + tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    env:
      # `prisma generate` and `import "@prisma/client"` want the variable to
      # exist; nothing in CI ever connects. This is not a real host.
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://ci:ci@127.0.0.1:5432/ci?schema=public
      # Keep the suite honest about being offline/deterministic.
      CI: "true"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # The Prisma client is generated, not committed. Type-checking `lib/**`
      # (and importing lib/mailer.ts from the dunning test) needs the generated
      # model types, so this must run before tsc and before the tests. Generation
      # reads prisma/schema.prisma only — it never contacts a database.
      - name: Generate Prisma client
        run: npx prisma generate

      - name: Typecheck (tsc --noEmit)
        run: |
          # tsc currently reports TS5097 for every `import … from "../lib/x.ts"`
          # in test/*.test.ts: the tests import with an explicit .ts extension
          # (which the `tsx --test` runner requires) while the tsconfig does not
          # set `allowImportingTsExtensions`. Those lines are the established,
          # pre-existing exception in this repo — everything else must be clean.
          #
          # The filter is deliberately narrower than the `grep -v "test/.*test.ts"`
          # convention used by hand: it drops ONLY TS5097 lines from test files, so
          # a genuine type error in a test still fails this job.
          npx tsc --noEmit > tsc.log 2>&1 || true
          grep -vE '^test/[^ ]+\.test\.ts\([0-9]+,[0-9]+\): error TS5097:' tsc.log > tsc-unexpected.log || true
          if [ -s tsc-unexpected.log ]; then
            echo "::error::tsc reported errors outside the known TS5097 test-import exception"
            cat tsc-unexpected.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "Typecheck clean ($(grep -c 'TS5097' tsc.log || true) known TS5097 test-import lines suppressed)."

      - name: Unit tests
        run: npm test

      - name: Upload typecheck log on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4

          name: tsc-log
          path: tsc.log

#!/bin/bash
# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment.
# Usage: ./scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref]
set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging

echo "==> Syncing staging to $REF"
git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"

echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1

echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2
npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true

echo "==> Building"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4

# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. Only .next needs to be writable by
# it (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable, and systemd
# injects .env as root. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon-staging/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon-staging/.env 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Restarting staging services"
systemctl restart nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
echo "==> Staging responds: HTTP $CODE (http://$(grep ^PUBLIC_IP .env | cut -d= -f2):8080)"
[ "$CODE" = "200" ] || { echo "STAGING UNHEALTHY"; exit 1; }
echo "==> Staging deploy complete"
